title: A high-resolution study of the double radio relic system in MACS J1752.0+4440
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A. 11 pages, 15 figures, 4 tables
summary: Radio relics are diffuse, extended synchrotron sources located at the outskirts of merging galaxy clusters. Their origin has been linked with shock waves injected into the intracluster medium, but the acceleration mechanism at the shock front is still under debate. Some clusters, like MACS J1752.0+4440, host a double relic system, with two relics found on opposite sides with respect to the cluster center. To investigate the acceleration mechanism that generates radio relics, we study the morphological and spectral properties of the double relic system in MACS J1752. We present new wideband radio continuum observations made with uGMRT and JVLA, and LOFAR data. We perform a detailed, high-resolution spectral analysis of the double relic system in MACS J1752, observing and characterizing substructures, particularly for the brighter relic. We find a double-peaked surface brightness and spectral index profile for the NE relic and identify a "bright bar" substructure. Moreover, we observed surprisingly flat integrated spectral indices for both relics, at $α_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathrm{NE}} = -0.91 \pm 0.06$ and $α_{\mathrm{int}}^{\mathrm{SW}} = -0.83 \pm 0.05$. We study the spatial variation of the spectral index, observing a coherent trend with the observed substructures. We estimate an injection Mach number of $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{NE}} = 3.1^{+0.1}_{-0.1}$ and $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{SW}} = 3.2^{+0.1}_{-0.1}$. By performing a spectral curvature analysis for both relics, generating color-color plots and a spectral curvature maps, we observe two "concave" spectra represented by positive spectral curvature, in contrast with particle population ageing models. The observed properties of the NE relic are not consistent with a simple scenario with a single shock front. Multiple shock surfaces, re-acceleration, and projection effects likely play a role in shaping the morphology of the relic.

AI.tldr: This study uses new radio observations to analyze the double relics in MACS J1752, revealing complex shock structures and acceleration mechanisms beyond simple models, with significant substructures and spectral characteristics indicating multiple shocks and re-acceleration.
AI.motivation: Understand the acceleration mechanism generating radio relics in galaxy clusters, focusing on the double relic system in MACS J1752.
AI.method: Conduct new wideband radio continuum observations using uGMRT, JVLA, and LOFAR; perform high-resolution spectral analysis, including spectral curvature and color-color plot analysis.
AI.result: Identified substructures such as double-peaked brightness and a bright bar in the NE relic; found flat integrated spectral indices indicating higher Mach numbers (~3.1-3.2); observed positive spectral curvature inconsistent with simple particle ageing models; concluded that multiple shock surfaces, re-acceleration, and projection effects influence relic morphology.
AI.conclusion: The NE relic's properties challenge the simple single shock front model, suggesting complex shock dynamics and acceleration processes in the double relic system of MACS J1752.

title: Pulsar scintillation studies with LOFAR III. Annual variations in PSR~J0814$+$7429
summary: The interstellar scintillation observed in radio pulsars arises from interference between electromagnetic waves scattered by electron density fluctuations in the turbulent interstellar plasma, providing a critical tool for probing the small-scale structure of the ionized interstellar medium and the pulsar system itself. The primary aim of this work is to study long-term scintillation variations for a bright and nearby pulsar, PSR J0814$+$7429, carried out from 2013 September to 2023 September with the LOw-Frequency ARray (LOFAR) High Band Antennae in the frequency range of 120 - 170 MHz. We derive the basic scintillation parameters, scintillation bandwidth ($Δν_{\rm d}$) and scintillation timescale ($Δτ_{\rm d}$), from the two-dimensional (2D) auto-covariance function of the dynamic spectra that are a 2D matrix of pulse intensity as a function of time and frequency. We present the long-term monitoring of $Δν_{\rm d}$ and $Δτ_{\rm d}$ for PSR J0814$+7429$, which shows a strong annual variation in the time series of the $Δτ_{\rm d}$. From our modeling of the annual variations of scintillation velocities, the scattering screen is anisotropic and located at $0.23\pm0.02$ kpc from the Earth, likely corresponding to the boundary of the Local Bubble.

AI.tldr: A decade-long LOFAR observation of pulsar PSR J0814+7429 reveals annual scintillation variations caused by an anisotropic scattering screen about 0.23 kpc away, likely at the Local Bubble's boundary.
AI.motivation: To study long-term scintillation variations in a bright and nearby pulsar to probe the small-scale structure of the ionized interstellar medium and the pulsar system.
AI.method: Monitoring the pulsar PSR J0814+7429 from 2013 to 2023 using LOFAR High Band Antennae at 120-170 MHz; deriving scintillation bandwidth and timescale from the 2D auto-covariance function of dynamic spectra.
AI.result: Observed strong annual variations in scintillation timescale; modeling indicates an anisotropic scattering screen located at 0.23±0.02 kpc, likely at the boundary of the Local Bubble.
AI.conclusion: Long-term monitoring reveals anisotropic scattering properties of the interstellar medium affecting PSR J0814+7429, with the scattering screen near the Local Bubble boundary.

title: What Are Pulsar Companions Made of? Using Gravitational Tides to Probe Their Compositions
summary: Low eccentricity, short orbital period pulsar companions may provide a probe to study novel dense and stable exoplanet internal compositions due to the potentially significant orbital evolution they experience caused by strong gravitational tides. We model the tidal characteristics such as apsidal motion constants, orbital precession, and tidal deformability for a variety of equations of state to be compared with values recovered via pulsar timing for a sample of four systems: PSR J1719-1438b, PSR J0636+5128b, PSR J2322+2650b, and PSR J1807-2459A b. With this method, we hope to place stringent limits on the chemical and structural composition of these objects. Through limiting the internal composition of pulsar companions, we aim to elucidate their unique history and formation.

AI.tldr: This paper models tidal effects on pulsar companions to constrain their internal composition, enabling a better understanding of their origin and structure through pulsar timing observations.
AI.motivation: To use low eccentricity, short orbital period pulsar companions as probes to study novel dense and stable exoplanet internal compositions affected by strong gravitational tides.
AI.method: Modeling tidal characteristics—including apsidal motion constants, orbital precession, and tidal deformability—across various equations of state and comparing these with pulsar timing data from four specific pulsar systems.
AI.result: Establishment of stringent limits on the chemical and structural composition of pulsar companions based on tidal characteristic analysis and observational data comparison.
AI.conclusion: Limiting the internal composition of pulsar companions provides insights into their unique formation history and evolutionary processes.

title: Spin effects in superfluidity, neutron matter and neutron stars
comment: Invited review article for Science Advances, 24 pages, 7 figures
summary: We review selected aspects of the interior physics of compact stars, focusing on the microscopic and macroscopic manifestations of spin, magnetic fields, and nucleonic superfluidity and superconductivity. Spin statistics of fermions allows quantum degeneracy pressure to determine the stability and global properties of neutron stars, whose structure depends sensitively on the strong interactions among baryons in dense matter. Using a generic meta-modeling framework based on an expansion of the nuclear energy density around the isospin-symmetric and saturation-density limits, we highlight how various lesser-known terms in this expansion affect compact-star observables and review multimessenger constraints on mass, radius, and moment of inertia. The influence of magnetic fields on dense matter is examined, showing that substantial effects in their structure require extremely strong fields, whereas lower fields are sufficient to affect their superfluid phases. At the mesoscopic scale, the coexistence of superfluid and superconducting components features vortex and flux-tube lattices, with pinning and mutual friction processes playing central roles in neutron-star rotational dynamics. We discuss unresolved issues concerning vortex structure, flux-tube configurations, and the origin of pulsar glitches and post-glitch relaxation. We also briefly address the possible emergence of deconfined quark phases in compact-star cores, including their color-superconducting properties, as well as the associated vortex structures and magnetic-field responses in such phases.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews how spin, magnetic fields, and nucleonic superfluidity/superconductivity impact neutron star interior physics and observables, discusses modeling methods and multimessenger constraints, and addresses open problems including vortex dynamics and quark matter phases.
AI.motivation: To understand how microscopic physics such as spin, magnetic fields, nucleonic superfluidity and superconductivity affect the interior structure and observable properties of compact stars like neutron stars.
AI.method: Review of theoretical approaches including a meta-modeling framework expanding nuclear energy density around isospin-symmetric and saturation-density limits, and examination of effects of magnetic fields and superfluid/superconducting phases on mesoscopic and macroscopic scales, combined with discussion of multimessenger observational constraints.
AI.result: Identification of critical roles played by spin statistics, strong baryonic interactions, magnetic fields, superfluid/superconducting vortex and flux-tube lattices in neutron star structure and dynamics; highlighting the need for extremely strong magnetic fields to impact bulk structure; elucidation of unresolved issues such as vortex and flux-tube configurations and pulsar glitches; and consideration of deconfined quark phases and color superconductivity in neutron star cores.
AI.conclusion: Compact star interior physics is significantly influenced by quantum statistical effects, strong nuclear interactions, and magnetic fields; the superfluid and superconducting phases with associated vortex and flux-tube dynamics crucially affect rotational behavior and glitch phenomena; future progress requires resolving outstanding questions on vortex structures and exploring quark-phase implications through multiphysics and multimessenger studies.

title: Cosmology-Independent Constraints on the Etherington Relation and SNeIa Absolute Magnitude Evolution from DESI-DR2
comment: 12 pages, 5 figures, to be submitted to PRD, comments welcomed
summary: We carry out a test of the fundamental Etherington relation (cosmic distance duality relation) which relates the luminosity distance $D_{\rm L}$ and angular diameter distance $D_{\rm A}$ in metric theories of gravity. We use the latest measurements of the angular diameter distance as a function of redshift from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Data Release 2 (DESI-DR2) and the luminosity distance from a variety of compilations of Supernovae of Type Ia (SNeIa). Our results indicate that these measurements are statistically consistent with the Etherington relation. In addition to providing a confirmation of the underlying assumptions of the Etherington relation, i.e., the metric nature of gravity, Lorentz invariance and photon number conservation, our results are also a stringent test of any residual systematic effects. We interpret the absence of evidence of any deviation from this relation to constrain the evolution of the absolute magnitude of SNeIa to $dM/dz = 0.07 \pm 0.07$ over and above the systematics that are already accounted for in the SNeIa analyses. We discuss how the Etherington relation can be used to constrain systematic parameters in the analyses of dynamical dark energy using geometric probes, to make it more robust against systematic effects.

AI.tldr: This paper tests the Etherington relation using DESI-DR2 angular diameter distances and Type Ia Supernova luminosity distances, confirming the relation holds and constraining supernova magnitude evolution and systematics in cosmological analyses.
AI.motivation: To test the fundamental Etherington relation which links luminosity and angular diameter distances, thereby validating key assumptions in metric theories of gravity and probing potential systematic effects in cosmological measurements.
AI.method: The study tested the Etherington relation by comparing the latest angular diameter distance data from DESI-DR2 with luminosity distance data from various compilations of Type Ia Supernovae across different redshifts.
AI.result: No deviations from the Etherington relation were found, allowing constraints on the evolution of the absolute magnitude of SNeIa at $dM/dz = 0.07 \pm 0.07$, and demonstrating that the relation can help control systematics in dynamical dark energy studies using geometric probes.
AI.conclusion: The measurements of angular diameter distance from DESI-DR2 and luminosity distance from SNeIa compilations are statistically consistent with the Etherington relation, confirming the metric nature of gravity, Lorentz invariance, and photon number conservation without detecting deviations.

title: Optical observations and atomic environment of supernova remnant G25.1-2.3
comment: 18 pages, 10 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: The supernova remnant (SNR) G25.1-2.3 was identified in the radio band during the Sino-German $λ$6 cm survey of the Galactic plane. We present a detailed investigation of the optical, HI, and CO emission towards the G25.1-2.3 to better understand its characteristics and environment. In this study, optical spectroscopic data of the remnant and its environment have been analysed for the first time, providing new insights into their emission properties. The Large Sky Area Multi-Object Fiber Spectroscopic Telescope (LAMOST) and 1.5-m Russian-Turkish Telescope (RTT150) data show variations across the observed regions, with [SII]/H$α$ ranging from 0.16 to 0.83. We identified shock-heated gas in the northern and southern regions and several photoionized regions around the SNR based on their [SII]/H$α$ ratios derived from spectra. The [SII]$λ$6716/$λ$6731 ratio observed in the northern region suggests electron densities ($n_{\rm e}$) ranging from 120 to 1030 cm$^{-3}$, whereas the southern regions show higher values, between 490 and 4500 cm$^{-3}$. The variations in the observed H$α$/H$β$ ratios indicate significant differences in extinction across the regions. H$α$ images obtained using the 1-m Turkish Telescope (T100) reveal optical emission in the northern and southern, characterized by filamentary and diffuse structures. We newly found a hole-like distribution of HI, whose spatial extent is roughly consistent with the diameter of the SNR. Based on radio data, we examine the evolutionary stage of G25.1-2.3 using the surface brightness-diameter ($Σ-D$) relation and the equipartition method.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a detailed multi-wavelength investigation of the supernova remnant G25.1-2.3, analyzing optical spectra, HI, CO, and radio data to characterize its emission properties, electron densities, extinction variations, morphology, and evolutionary stage.
AI.motivation: To better understand the characteristics and environment of the supernova remnant G25.1-2.3 through multi-wavelength observations, including optical spectroscopy, HI, CO, and radio data.
AI.method: Analysis of optical spectroscopic data from LAMOST and RTT150 to study emission line ratios; imaging with the 1-m Turkish Telescope for optical morphology; examination of HI distribution; and application of the surface brightness-diameter ($Σ-D$) relation and equipartition method using radio data.
AI.result: Identification of shock-heated gas and photoionized regions based on [SII]/Hα ratios; determination of electron densities from [SII] line ratios showing regional variation; detection of extinction variations from Hα/Hβ ratios; discovery of optical filamentary and diffuse emission structures; detection of an HI hole coincident with the SNR's spatial extent; assessment of the SNR's evolutionary stage via radio data.
AI.conclusion: The multi-wavelength study revealed detailed physical and environmental properties of SNR G25.1-2.3, including varying electron densities, extinction, and gas excitation mechanisms, as well as morphological and HI structural features consistent with the remnant's evolutionary status.

title: Return to the Great Attractor: Strong Evidence for a Steradian-sized Flow Converging at $\sim$70 Mpc within the GA Supercluster and Aligned with the CMB Dipole
summary: We used the FourStar near-IR camera on Magellan-Baade to obtain high S/N H-Band imaging of 66 galaxies with radial velocities of 2000 < V < 5000 km/s. Our goal was to use the superior distance measurements of surface-brightness-fluctuations (SBF) to derive ``peculiar velocities'' to test claims that the CMB dipole anisotropy, equivalent to $\approx$600 km/s with respect to the Local Group, arises from a 'local' overdensity in the galaxy/dark-matter distribution -- the Great Attractor. SBF's ability to measure distances with 5% accuracy confirms a strong flow over a steradian of the sky peaking at Vpec $\sim$ 1000 km/s and converging to zero at D $\approx$70 Mpc from the Local Group. The modest spatial extent of this flow $R_V$ $\sim$ 5000 km/s is consistent with the original Great Attractor model (a diameter D $\sim$ 140 Mpc), as well as the magnitude and direction of the CMB dipole anisotropy, and the power spectrum of CMB fluctuations -- the latter two arguably the most secure measurements in astrophysics. In contrast, our results are at-odds with reports of comparable amplitude 'bulk flows' on scales of hundreds of Mpc that themselves may be inconsistent with the expected fluctuations in the CMB for a $Λ$CDM universe. We contend that only distance-estimators as accurate as SBF are able settle the question of whether the CMB dipole arises from the gravitational influence of large-scale structure within, or without $\sim$100 Mpc of the Local Group.

AI.tldr: Using precise distance measurements from near-IR imaging and SBF, this study confirms a local peculiar velocity flow matching the Great Attractor model and the CMB dipole anisotropy, challenging claims of large-scale bulk flows and emphasizing the need for accurate distance estimators to understand the origin of the CMB dipole.
AI.motivation: To test whether the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) dipole anisotropy, indicating a velocity of about 600 km/s relative to the Local Group, is caused by a local overdensity known as the Great Attractor.
AI.method: Used FourStar near-infrared camera on Magellan-Baade telescope to obtain high signal-to-noise H-Band imaging of 66 galaxies with radial velocities between 2000 and 5000 km/s, employing surface-brightness-fluctuations (SBF) for precise distance measurement with ~5% accuracy.
AI.result: Detected a strong peculiar velocity flow peaking at about 1000 km/s over a sky steradian, converging to zero at approximately 70 Mpc from the Local Group, consistent with the spatial extent and scale of the Great Attractor, and matching the magnitude/direction of the CMB dipole anisotropy and CMB power spectrum. These findings contradict reports of large-scale bulk flows extending over hundreds of Mpc.
AI.conclusion: The gravitational influence causing the CMB dipole anisotropy likely originates within ~100 Mpc around the Local Group, supporting the Great Attractor model, and precise distance measurements like SBF are crucial for resolving this question.

title: Cosmological Constraints from GW-FRB Associations without Redshift Measurements for LIGO-Virgo and Cosmic Explorer
summary: The potential association between gravitational waves (GWs) and fast radio bursts (FRBs) offers a unique multi-messenger probe for cosmology. In this paper, we develop a redshift-independent framework to constrain cosmological parameters using the luminosity distance - dispersion measure relation, accounting for realistic astrophysical uncertainties. We perform a comprehensive comparative analysis across different GWs detector sensitivities and modeling assumptions. Specifically, we investigate the performance of the current LIGO-Virgo (LV) network (at $z < 0.2$) versus the future Cosmic Explorer (CE). Our study further evaluates the impact of different dispersion measure (DM) distributions -- specifically the corrected Macquart's PDF (Zhuge+2025) and the log-normal distribution -- and explores the influence of including or excluding host galaxy DM contributions. Using realistic simulated observations, we find that while the current LV network lacks the precision to provide meaningful constraints, CE will enable high-precision cosmology. Even without spectroscopic redshifts, CE observations can effectively break parameter degeneracies and robustly constrain both cosmology and host galaxy parameters. These results highlight the necessity of next-generation detectors.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a redshift-independent method using GW and FRB observations to constrain cosmology, showing that while current detectors are insufficient, future observatories like Cosmic Explorer can provide high-precision, spectroscopic-redshift-free cosmological measurements.
AI.motivation: To explore the potential of gravitational waves (GWs) and fast radio bursts (FRBs) as a multi-messenger probe for cosmology, overcoming the limitations of current methods by developing a redshift-independent framework.
AI.method: Developing a framework based on the luminosity distance - dispersion measure relation that incorporates realistic astrophysical uncertainties; performing comparative analyses across current (LIGO-Virgo) and future (Cosmic Explorer) GW detectors; evaluating different dispersion measure distributions and host galaxy DM contributions using simulated observations.
AI.result: The current LIGO-Virgo network at low redshifts lacks the precision for meaningful cosmological constraints, whereas the future Cosmic Explorer will enable high-precision cosmology, breaking parameter degeneracies and constraining both cosmological and host galaxy parameters without requiring spectroscopic redshifts.
AI.conclusion: Next-generation gravitational wave detectors like Cosmic Explorer are essential for leveraging the GW-FRB multi-messenger approach to achieve robust and precise cosmological constraints independent of redshift measurements.

title: Inferring population III star properties from the 21-cm global signal
summary: Investigating the properties of the first stars in the universe is essential, yet it remains an open question. One way to explore these stars is by examining their effects on the surrounding gas during the epoch of reionization. In this study, we investigate whether the 21-cm global signal can constrain the typical mass and star formation efficiency of first-generation stars. We perform semi-numerical simulations that include the escape fraction of ionizing photons, which depends on stellar and halo masses, as well as the heating structure surrounding a halo that hosts the first star, determined by radiation hydrodynamics (RHD) simulations. By applying Fisher analysis, while accounting for foreground emissions, we demonstrate that future observations with instruments such as the Radio Experiment for the Analysis of Cosmic Hydrogen (REACH) could provide meaningful constraints on these properties.

AI.tldr: This study demonstrates that upcoming 21-cm observations can constrain mass and star formation efficiency of the first stars by leveraging advanced simulations and Fisher analysis, aiding our understanding of cosmic dawn.
AI.motivation: Understanding the properties of the first stars is crucial for comprehending the early universe, but these properties remain largely unknown.
AI.method: The study uses semi-numerical simulations incorporating variable escape fractions of ionizing photons dependent on stellar and halo masses, alongside radiation hydrodynamics simulations to model the heating surrounding first-star-hosting halos. It then applies Fisher analysis considering foreground emissions to examine constraining power of 21-cm global signal observations.
AI.result: The analysis shows that future 21-cm signal observations from instruments like REACH can effectively constrain typical mass and star formation efficiency of first-generation stars.
AI.conclusion: The 21-cm global signal is a viable probe to constrain fundamental properties of first-generation stars, improving our understanding of star formation during the epoch of reionization.

title: Single field slow-roll inflation with step uplift to $n_s=1$
summary: The early dark energy resolution of Hubble tension seems to be suggesting a scale-invariant Harrison-Zeldovich spectrum of primordial scalar perturbation, i.e. $n_s=1$ ($|n_s-1|\sim {\cal O}(0.001)$) for $H_0\sim 73$km/s/Mpc. In this work, we propose a possibility to acquire $n_s=1$ in single field slow-roll models of inflation. In our consideration, the potential of inflaton during inflation still preserve the shape of well-known single field inflation models in deep slow-roll region, but inflation ends suddenly due to a large step of inflaton potential. In particular, we investigate the implication of our scheme for chaotic inflation and Starobinski inflation, and show how they can be compatible with the observation for $n_s=1$.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a modification to single field slow-roll inflation models by including a sudden end to inflation through a potential step, allowing chaotic and Starobinski inflation to produce a scale-invariant spectrum ($n_s=1$) consistent with early dark energy explanations of the Hubble tension.
AI.motivation: Addressing the Hubble tension by reconciling it with a scale-invariant Harrison-Zeldovich spectrum ($n_s=1$) of primordial scalar perturbations implied by early dark energy models.
AI.method: Propose a single field slow-roll inflation model where the inflaton potential maintains a conventional shape in the deep slow-roll region but ends abruptly due to a large step in the potential, analyzing its application to chaotic and Starobinski inflation.
AI.result: Demonstrated that chaotic inflation and Starobinski inflation can be consistent with observational data when modified to include a sudden end of inflation, achieving $n_s=1$ compatible with the Hubble tension resolution.
AI.conclusion: It is possible to realize a scale-invariant scalar spectral index $n_s=1$ within single field slow-roll inflation models by introducing a sudden end of inflation via a step in the inflaton potential, making these models consistent with observations related to the Hubble tension.

title: Which filaments matter: the relative scalings of anisotropic infall
summary: Dark-matter haloes do not form in isolation but within the surrounding cosmic web. By the time a halo begins to collapse, its larger-scale environment has typically collapsed along two axes, forming filaments that channel anisotropic infall toward the halo. In this work, we derive from first principles the characteristic Lagrangian scale ratio at which such an anisotropic tidal field most strongly influences halo formation. Specifically, we identify the inflection point of the conditional probability that the tidal field, smoothed on a scale Rsd, undergoes two-dimensional compression, given the presence of a density peak of rarity nu on a smaller scale Rpk. For a standard LambdaCDM cosmology, we find (Rsd/Rpk)infl = 2.2 + (nu-2.5) for Rpk corresponding to a tophat filter of 8Mpc/h. This result implies that the anisotropic tidal influence on a collapsing halo typically extends to 2-3 times the size of its Lagrangian patch. Recast as a function of formation redshift z, the characteristic filament scale around 2.5 sigma peaks can be approximated by Rsd(z) = 31 /(2+(1+z)**2)Mpc/h. We provide practical scaling laws for selecting dynamically relevant smoothing scales in large-scale surveys and for setting initial patch sizes in high-resolution zoom simulations.

AI.tldr: This paper derives the characteristic scale at which anisotropic tidal fields from filaments affect dark-matter halo formation, finding that this influence extends 2-3 times the halo's Lagrangian size and providing practical scaling laws for cosmological applications.
AI.motivation: To understand how the anisotropic tidal field within the cosmic web influences dark-matter halo collapse, specifically quantifying the scale over which this influence is significant.
AI.method: Derived the characteristic Lagrangian scale ratio analytically from first principles by identifying the inflection point of the conditional probability that the tidal field undergoes two-dimensional compression, conditioned on density peaks, in a LambdaCDM cosmology framework.
AI.result: Established that the characteristic scale ratio (Rsd/Rpk)infl is approximately 2.2 + (nu-2.5) for relevant density peaks, implying filament influence extends 2-3 times the halo's Lagrangian scale; additionally provided a redshift-dependent scaling law for filament scale applicable to simulations and surveys.
AI.conclusion: The anisotropic tidal field influencing halo formation extends typically 2-3 times beyond the halo's Lagrangian scale, with a characteristic scale ratio derived from first principles and a practical formula linked to formation redshift.

title: Mapping the redshift drift at various redshifts through cosmography
summary: The redshift drift provides a kinematic test of the cosmic expansion history through the slow time variation of the redshift of comoving sources. Motivated by the expected Sandage-Loeb measurements from future facilities, we investigate the drift within a cosmographic framework, modeling the Hubble rate through both a second-order Taylor expansion and a $(2,1)$ Padé approximant. We constrain the cosmographic parameters $(H_0,q_0,j_0)$ by combining Pantheon+ and SH0ES type Ia supernovae with gamma-ray bursts and then examine the impact of adding baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from the second DESI data release. The resulting constraints are used to construct a mock Sandage-Loeb catalog, after which the analyses are repeated including the simulated drift data. In this way, we assess the internal consistency of the reconstructed background rather than perform an independent forecast. Accordingly, we find that, for the SNeIa+GRB analysis, the Taylor reconstruction is compatible at the $1σ$ level with the $ω_0ω_1$CDM scenario, whereas the Padé parameterization improves the agreement of $q_0$ with the $Λ$CDM paradigm. Once DESI BAO data are included, the agreement with the reference background models weakens to the $2σ$ level. The addition of the mock Sandage-Loeb sample mainly tightens the bounds on $q_0$ and $j_0$, with moderate shifts in the central values. We finally compare the reconstructed redshift drift with the corresponding behavior predicted by the $Λ$CDM and $ω_0ω_1$CDM scenarios.

AI.tldr: This study uses cosmographic expansions to analyze redshift drift with current SNeIa, GRB, and BAO data plus simulated Sandage-Loeb measurements, finding improved parameter constraints but moderate tension between models upon including BAO data.
AI.motivation: To investigate the redshift drift as a kinematic probe of cosmic expansion history, motivated by expected future Sandage-Loeb measurements.
AI.method: Cosmographic modeling of the Hubble rate via second-order Taylor expansion and (2,1) Pade approximant, constraining cosmographic parameters using Pantheon+, SH0ES SNeIa, GRB, and DESI BAO data, and constructing a mock Sandage-Loeb catalog for consistency checks.
AI.result: Taylor reconstruction aligns with ω₀ω₁CDM at 1σ, Pade approximation improves q₀ agreement with ΛCDM, inclusion of DESI BAO loosens model agreement to 2σ; mock Sandage-Loeb data tightens constraints on q₀ and j₀ with moderate parameter shifts.
AI.conclusion: Cosmographic reconstructions using current and simulated data provide a consistent but not definitive validation of standard cosmic expansion models, with Sandage-Loeb data enhancing parameter constraints but revealing mild tensions upon inclusion of DESI BAO data.

title: UNIONS-3500 Weak Lensing: II. B-mode validation for cosmic shear
comment: 11 pages, 8 figures, to be submitted to A&A
summary: At Stage-III sensitivities, cosmic shear $B$ modes unambiguously indicate systematic contamination and are often used to inform data selection and scale cuts for cosmological inference. We validate $B$ modes for the Ultraviolet Near-Infrared Optical Northern Survey (UNIONS)-3500 (2894 deg$^2$, $n_\mathrm{eff} \approx 5.0$ arcmin$^{-2}$) using three $E$/$B$-separable statistics: pure-mode correlation functions $ξ_\pm^{\mathrm{B}}(θ)$, Complete Orthogonal Sets of $E$/$B$-mode Integrals (COSEBI) $B$-mode amplitudes $B_n$, and harmonic-space power spectra $C_\ell^{BB}$. For each statistic, we compute probability-to-exceed (PTE) values over a two-dimensional grid of scale-cut boundaries; our adopted cuts lie in broad stable regions of acceptable PTE. $B$-mode detections and PTE failures on initial catalog versions led us to investigate galaxy size cuts and stellar halo masking. After cuts, all three statistics pass the null test (minimum PTE $= 0.18$). Before scale cuts, we measure an oscillatory COSEBI $B$-mode pattern consistent with repeating additive shear bias, a detector-level effect seen across multiple Stage-III surveys including CFHTLenS, which used the same MegaCam camera; scale cuts that exclude the charge-coupled device (CCD) angular scale suppress it. Although these statistics probe the same two-point shear field, scale cuts in one do not map exactly onto cuts in another, because their respective filter functions weight angular scales differently. The most conservative validation therefore requires scale and sample selections that pass null tests across all frameworks simultaneously, an approach that applies directly to Stage-IV surveys where systematic errors dominate.

AI.tldr: This paper validates B-mode contamination in the UNIONS-3500 cosmic shear survey using three statistical methods, identifying and mitigating detector-level systematics through strategic scale and sample cuts. It highlights the need for multi-statistic null tests to ensure robust cosmological inferences in current and future weak lensing surveys.
AI.motivation: To validate and characterize cosmic shear B modes as indicators of systematic contamination in large-scale Stage-III weak lensing surveys, and to inform data selection and scale cuts for robust cosmological inference.
AI.method: Applied three E/B-separable statistics—pure-mode B correlation functions, COSEBI B-mode amplitudes, and harmonic-space B-mode power spectra—to the UNIONS-3500 dataset, assessing probability-to-exceed (PTE) values over scale-cut grids to identify stable null-test passes and investigated galaxy size cuts and stellar halo masking to mitigate systematics.
AI.result: After applying optimized scale and sample cuts, all three statistics passed null tests with minimum PTE=0.18, detecting and suppressing oscillatory B-mode patterns consistent with known additive shear biases linked to CCD-level detector effects, demonstrating the necessity of coordinated scale and sample selections for consistent systematic error control.
AI.conclusion: The study establishes that rigorous validation of cosmic shear B modes using multiple E/B-separable statistics and carefully chosen scale and sample cuts effectively identifies and mitigates systematic contamination. This multi-framework approach is essential for controlling systematics in both Stage-III and forthcoming Stage-IV cosmological weak lensing surveys.
